name: Ember & Oak Coffee
tagline: Small-batch coffee, roasted the slow way.

essence.mission: Make the morning ritual feel worth slowing down for.
essence.positioning: For home brewers who care about flavour, Ember & Oak is the neighbourhood roaster that ships beans within 48 hours of roasting, unlike supermarket coffee that sits on shelves for months.

audience.name: The weekend brewer
audience.description: 25-40, owns a pour-over or espresso machine, follows coffee creators, buys beans online.

do: Explain one idea at a time
examples: Fresh beans taste like fruit. Old beans taste like cardboard. That's the whole secret.
Sour shot? Grind a little finer and pull it again. Coffee forgives you if you go slow.
Grind right before you brew. That smell when the beans crack open is flavour you'd otherwise lose.

visual.imagery: Warm morning light, close-ups of hands and steam, matte brown and cream tones, shallow depth of field.

motion.notes: Slow fades and gentle rises. Nothing bounces.

narrator.description: Calm, friendly, 30s, light British accent, sounds like a barista talking across the counter.

audio.music: Lo-fi acoustic guitar, 80-90 BPM, warm and unobtrusive.
